  ∀ (g : ℕ → α), 
    (∀ i, g i ∈ s) →  -- g is a sequence in s
    (∀ i j, r i j → i ≠ j) →  -- g is a bad sequence (no relations between distinct elements)
    (∀ i < n, g i = f i) →  -- g agrees with f on first n terms
    ¬(∃ (g' : ℕ → α), (∀ i, g' i ∈ s) ∧ (∀ i j, r i j → i ≠ j) ∧ (∀ i < n, g' i = f i) ∧ g' n ≠ g n ∧ rk (g' n) < rk (f n)) := by sorry
